summary: Rabbi Tawil examines the beginning of the rebellion of Avshalom against his father, King David, in Shemuel Bet chapter 15. The class details how Avshalom used his charisma and public presence to win the hearts of the people before using a false vow as a pretext to travel to Chevron to launch his coup. Rabbi Tawil also discusses the significance of the shofar as a symbol of crowning a king and the rabbinic caution regarding the phrase 'lech beshalom'.
questions: Why did Avshalom choose to start his rebellion in Chevron?
What does the phrase 'lech beshalom' imply according to the rabbis?
Why was it permissible to bring a korban outside of Yerushalayim at that time?
How did Avshalom win the hearts of the people of Israel?
What is the significance of the shofar in the context of crowning a king?
